title: two-week-focus-ledger-outcomes-zoe-ramirez
content:
Quick note: trying a slightly different format for tracking outcomes this sprint — outcome-first, then signals, then tiny experiments. Keep it compact so I actually update it twice a week.

Objective (2 weeks): Reduce mean tail latency for interactive routing by 12% for 1-2s requests while keeping token-cost within 95% of baseline.
Key result (leading): average p95 latency on staging for the small-chat route drops from 720ms -> <=635ms.
Key result (lagging): production error-rate due to timeouts decreases by 20% week-over-week.

Why this matters (one line): fewer tail latency spikes improves conversation quality and decreases fallback to smaller models, saving units and reducing customer-visible failures.

Signals I'll watch (quick):
- p50/p95/p99 (staging) for small-chat route (daily)
- Token cost per 1k requests (rolling 7d)
- # fallbacks triggered to fallback-model on canary (alerts)
- Manual sniff test: 5 user conversations sampled Wed/Fri (qual)

Micro experiments (run in parallel, quick wins first):
1) KV cache warm-up tweak (A/B 50/50 on canary)
   - Hypothesis: prefetching common system prefixes for parallel requests reduces first-token latency by ~30ms
   - Safety: limited to 10% of traffic in canary, immediate rollback flag if error-rate > 0.5%
   - Implementation notes: reuse existing cache layer, add warm-up hook in routing code (PR #834).
2) Dynamic batching policy change: shorter max-batch-wait for <256-token requests
   - Hypothesis: for small requests batching delay dominates; smaller wait reduces latency with minimal throughput loss
   - Quick metric: avg batch size and per-token cost delta after 24h
3) Fallback routing heuristic tweak: allow single retry to regional variant before global fallback
   - Hypothesis: regional retry reduces fallbacks due to transient network blips

Check-ins (what I actually did this week):
- Mon: instrumented p95 logging and added per-route p95 metric to the dashboard. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/834
- Tue: sketched warm-up hook and ran a local microbench with synthetic prefixes; saw ~22ms median improvement in first token (small sample).
- Wed: deployed canary with KV warm-up to 5% traffic; watchlist: p95 and error-rate. Noticed small uptick in CPU on canary nodes (+3%).
- Thu: tune max-batch-wait from 12ms -> 6ms for <256-token queue in staging; observed p95 reduce by ~18ms but throughput dip of ~4% at peak. Need to quantify cost impact.
- Fri: quick user sniff test (5 conversations) — subjective latency felt snappier in 3/5. Collected timestamps.

Open questions / risks (short bullets):
- Is the CPU uptick from warm-up hook causing more contention on shared nodes? What happens under sustained QPS?
- Does the batching change push more work onto the network layer (more RPCs), increasing infra cost?
- Need an SLA-safe rollback plan if both changes together cause unexpected tail effects.

Quick math (back-of-envelope):
- Current small-chat p95 staging: 720ms. Target 12% = 86ms reduction -> 634ms.
- Warm-up alone (local) ~22ms median; batching change ~18ms. Combined naive sum 40ms — short of 86ms but we might get nonlinear benefits (reduced retries).
- Cost check: throughput dip ~4% could increase per-token cost by ~3.5% depending on utilization. Keep within 95% baseline is tight.

Action items (this sprint):
- A1: Expand canary warm-up to 20% if error-rate stays <0.3% and CPU anomaly <=5% (owner: me).
- A2: Run 72-hour staging load test with combined changes to observe tail under sustained QPS (owner: Arjun).
- A3: Add rollback runbook steps to the canary dashboard and set an automated cutoff for fallbacks > 1% (owner: me).
- A4: Calculate cost delta from batching change using historical peak traces (owner: Maya).

Personal rhythm notes (meta):
- Update this ledger Thu mornings (short) and Sun evenings (deeper reflection).
- Keep experiments bite-sized — if an experiment requires >4 dev hours, break into sub-experiments.
- Capture subjective user checks with a quick timestamped note into #perf-sniffers.

Retro prompts for next run (questions to answer):
- Which signal predicted production fallbacks earliest? (p95 staging? error spikes? retries?)
- Which micro-experiment delivered best latency per unit-cost saved?
- How did the canary CPU behavior correlate with request distribution (size/sequence length)?

Notes-to-self / friction log (short):
- Need a simpler dashboard slice that shows p95 by token-length bucket (0-64, 65-256, 256-1024) — current dashboard lacks this granularity.
- Reminder: talk to infra about node CPU headroom and possible pinning options.
- Follow-up: schedule 30-min sync with Maya + Arjun next Tue.

Tiny wins to celebrate (motivation):
- Cleaned up the canary deploy checklist and removed 3 manual steps. Felt good.
- Local bench showed measurable first-token improvement on synthetic prefixes.

End note: keep this ledger action-oriented. If an idea doesn't have a next step, it's a note, not an experiment.

-- ZR
